boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Single source for the accepted navigation action count. The acceptance lanes must not pin how many menus the product has. A menu count is only determinate once a concrete role is locked, because different roles see different contracted surfaces. The policy therefore declares which accepted role is under test and which versioned contract field is authoritative for that role (``navigation_policy.action_count_authority``); this module resolves the count from that declaration, so adding or removing a contracted product entry (or switching the principal role) is a contract data change rather than an edit to a release constant. Mechanism, not number: * a policy that pins ``min_actions``/``max_actions``/``action_count`` fails; * an authority that is not a versioned contract in exact mode fails; * a principal role with no declared authoritative surface fails closed; * a role surface whose declared count disagrees with its locked identity list fails; * an unresolvable or non-positive resolved value fails.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Bind the acceptance surface to every code change. A change is only "covered" when the paths it touches are declared in the acceptance evolution registry and the acceptance suites that registry requires are either: * executed by the same governed lane (contract/governance suites), or * backed by an exact-head evidence manifest produced by a real runtime run. The plan half is deterministic and runs in every PR/local lane. The evidence half is fail-closed and is required by ``make pr.merge``. HEAD is provenance, not an invalidation key: a suite may reuse evidence from an ancestor only while its declared input fingerprint and evidence bytes are identical. Any changed suite layer still has to be executed at the evaluated head. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 binding/evidence failure, 2 usage or registry error.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed consistency guard for the .agent run/goal ledger. Rule: the ledger must be internally consistent, so "goal and run status are out of sync" is a mechanically detected defect instead of a recurring manual audit. * a terminal run (completed/superseded) must not leave a non-terminal goal behind; * the active-run index must point at an existing, branch-matching, non-terminal run; * every run record keeps a canonical status and resolvable goal/record paths; * every goal declares an id, a status and, when it names a run, a resolvable path. Legacy receipts written before the goal/record schema are pinned in ``LEGACY_ARCHIVAL_RUNS``. Their bytes are historical evidence and are not rewritten to satisfy the current schema; the pin records the exact raw status so a silent lifecycle rewrite is still detected. A new legacy-shaped record that is not pinned fails this guard. Owner-kept ledger residuals are pinned with their recorded authority. The pins are ratchets: the on-disk set must equal the pinned set exactly, so a new residual cannot appear silently and a closed one must be removed here in the same change. This guard only reads the .agent ledger and never mutates it.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Runtime half of the contract SLO telemetry gap. Run with: make verify.backend.contract_slo_telemetry.runtime This script is executed by ``odoo shell`` against the isolated contract-lifecycle profile (project ``sc-contract-lifecycle-v1``, database ``sc_contract_lifecycle``). It drives real ``ui.contract.v2`` deliveries through the production handler, captures the ``contractSlo`` line the production sink actually emits, and binds each observation back through the declaration consumer (``contract_slo_telemetry``), so a passing run means the runtime delivery path emitted a schema-valid, identity-complete observation rather than that a string merely appeared. Baseline first: the normal path must emit ``success`` before any injected state is treated as detected. Injection proof lives outside this script (neuter the emission boundary, prove zero lines, restore byte-identical); this script only records the healthy baseline into a machine-readable report consumed by the host-side schema guard.
